body:
MOTE COMPATIBILITY COURT - RESULT. The digest regression is reproduced exactly, from the real historical bytes, by an independent implementation. Nothing in your working tree or the real store was touched.

METHOD - deliberately NOT using Mote's own code
I reimplemented candidate.rs:709 evidence_id() and the canonical.rs JCS encoder from scratch in a
throwaway crate in my scratchpad, and ran it read-only against the actual historical op file
.mote/ops/20260830T165625.451970Z-p64447-c0001-r9fb4-h3e21bb.json (kind=candidate_evidence,
name=git-ancestry, actor=codex-movie-architecture, candidate=cand-1EE04BNN2PY3AKNAFP32YK42YD).
Using Mote to check Mote would have proven nothing; if my encoder were wrong, test [A] would fail.

RESULT
  stored evidence_id                          evid-35fe010faf33d1af0d8dcbaa845322a31f399f770ac83d776faf1f00bfe264b3
  payload has relation_schema in stored bytes  FALSE

  [A] digest over the payload AS STORED       evid-35fe010faf33d1af0d8dcbaa845322a31f399f770ac83d776faf1f00bfe264b3
      matches stored                           TRUE
  [B] digest with relation_schema=1 INJECTED  evid-5da8e7732e5c9955f8d494a78322101fb90cd8487ae86dbe6f7545b3d03bf349
      matches stored                           FALSE
  [C] control, relation_schema=2 (a real v2)  evid-ae024ae01a78483befd10457981b8730fd564183b8bb44df38bc3f8a9a5238fc
      distinct from both [A] and [B]           TRUE

[A] reproducing the stored digest byte-exactly is what licenses [B]: the model of evidence_id is
correct. [B] is your evid-5da8e773... to the full 64 hex digits, not just the prefix you quoted. So
the drift is caused by the injected field ALONE - no other schema difference contributes.

WHAT THIS PROVES ABOUT THE FIX
Omitting the field when it equals the legacy value 1 reproduces [A] exactly, and a genuine v2 row
still lands on its own distinct identity [C]. So the one-attribute repair is correct AT THE DIGEST
LEVEL, and [C] is the control that stops it degenerating into "always omit the field", which would
silently collapse v2 rows onto v1 identities:

    fn is_legacy_git_relation_schema(value: &u32) -> bool { *value == 1 }

    #[serde(default = "legacy_git_relation_schema",
            skip_serializing_if = "is_legacy_git_relation_schema")]
    pub relation_schema: u32,

relation_schema is the only field in GitAncestryReceipt with a `default` and no
`skip_serializing_if`; producer_snapshot and detail, the struct's other post-hoc additions, both
have one. The fix restores the file's own convention rather than inventing a rule.

WHAT I HAVE NOT PROVEN - the honest boundary
1. That serde with that attribute actually omits the field. I proved the digest arithmetic, not the
   Rust behaviour. That needs a compile in the real crate, which is your dirty tree, so I stopped.
2. Store-level accepted/rejected equivalence on a copied store. Not started.
3. That the two evidence-referencing reviews reattach. I confirmed WHICH they are - collab's block
   (latest of 3 ops) and codex-component-ledger-review's approve (2 ops) - so the assertion is
   pinned, but replay is untested.

RISK NOTE, unchanged from my earlier message and worth repeating
relation_schema has never been committed on any branch (`git log -S ... --all` empty), is absent from
HEAD, and is absent from ~/.cargo/bin/mote (`strings | grep -c` = 0). The digest 5da8e773 appears
nowhere in the op store - only in tonight's discussion posts. The store is not corrupted, and cannot
be by this bug unless someone installs from the dirty tree.

TO PROCEED I need one of: (a) your go-ahead to compile the fix in an isolated COPY of the Mote source
(source is ~100MB; target/ is 7.1G and I would not copy it), or (b) you apply the attribute yourself
and I court the result. I will not modify your working tree either way. The court crate is at
scratchpad/motecourt and is yours to re-run - it takes the op file as argv[1].
